definition: Hiatus means a break or gap in continuity.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word hiatus. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know hiatus should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The bakery's window sign apologizes for a two-month hiatus while the ovens are rebuilt, and promises the sourdough will be back.
A pause is the mildest rung — over in moments, barely denting the flow; a hiatus opens a real gap, measured in months or years.
A cessation goes further than a hiatus: a hiatus ends with the thread picked up again, while a cessation closes the activity down for good.

A gap is the all-purpose opening in continuity — in a fence, a career, a data set. A hiatus is a particular kind of gap: a break in something serial, usually a long one, where the run is understood to continue afterward. Every hiatus is a gap; most gaps are not hiatuses.

An interlude is a stretch between two parts of something, and it brings content and a character of its own — the music between acts, the comic scene between battles. A hiatus is empty by contrast: the run simply stops, and the gap holds nothing until the thread resumes.
the unbroken flow itself
a stretch with no gap anywhere in it

Latin hiare, to gape, left almost nothing else in everyday English — its other descendants are botanists' and doctors' technical terms. So let the borrowed word carry its own picture: a gap with the same thing on both sides of it.
Hiatus means a break or gap in continuity.

The two chess players' correspondence game ran from 1969 to 2004 with one hiatus: nine years in the middle, after a move mailed to Buenos Aires never arrived and each man quietly assumed the other had given up.
A granddaughter found the unanswered postcard in a drawer in 1987, posted it with a note, and the game picked up at move 31 as though nothing had happened.
Hiatus is the right word because it means a break or gap in continuity — the game was never over, merely interrupted, and both the before and the after belong to one continuous whole.
A pause lasts moments; a hiatus can swallow years; but both differ from an ending, because a hiatus implies the thread will be, or at least could be, taken up again.

Hiatus is the dignified word for a long interruption in something serial — a career, a publication, a friendship — and it often appears in the idiom "on hiatus." Keep pause for seconds, recess for scheduled breaks of courts and legislatures, and lull for an unplanned quiet spell; hiatus claims a real gap in a run that is understood to continue.

For ninety-one years the ferry crossed the strait every morning, war and weather notwithstanding.
Then the engine gave out, the parts proved unmakeable, and the service entered what the harbor board carefully called a hiatus.
The word was chosen over 'closure' after two hours of debate, because the board wanted no one to think the crossing was finished.
For three years the slip stood empty.
Islanders mailed the board rivets, sketches, and once an entire salvaged engine of the wrong size.
When the refitted boat finally sounded its horn, the crowd on the dock behaved less like customers than like a family meeting a ship home.
